previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of systolic heart failure, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and alcoholic cirrhosis was admitted for hyponatremia and nausea. She had been drinking excess water due to fear of kidney failure, leading to polydipsia and low sodium. Fluid restriction improved her sodium levels, and she was restarted on torsemide for volume overload. She experienced an episode of chest pain, prompting cardiac testing that showed reduced ejection fraction on nuclear stress test; carvedilol was increased and imdur started. Hypertension and hyperkalemia led to dose adjustments in irbesartan. Her condition stabilized, and she was discharged home with instructions on fluid limits, daily weights, and cardiology follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
===================================
PRIMARY REASON FOR HOSPITALIZATION
===================================
Ms. ___ was admitted for hyponatremia and hyperkalemia found 
on routine labs at her PCP's office. She was referred to the ED 
and then admitted for further management.

Her hyponatremia was multifactorial in etiology: likely due to 
natriuresis from torsemide and hyperkalemia likely from 
hypoaldosteronism secondary to irbesartan use. She was given 1 L 
NS; her torsemide, sodium bicarb (patient was taking once a day, 
not BID as prescribed), and irbesartan were held during current 
hospitalization. Her Na trended up from 123 on admission to 131 
on discharge, and her K trended down to 4.5. She remained 
hemodynamically stable and euvolemic during her hospital stay. 
On discharge, she was started on amlodipine and advised to take 
torsemide 5 mg every other day.

Her weight upon discharge was 185 pounds, and should be a good 
dry weight for her moving forward. Her irbesartan and sodium 
bicarb were discontinued (it seems she can not tolerate ACEi or 
___ at this time due to hyperkalemia, and with her CKD stage III 
and normal bicarb level, there appeared to be no indication for 
sodium bicarb at this time). She will monitor her volume status 
by weighing herself daily, and was also advised that the 
amlodipine may lead to some ___ edema. She is very concerned 
about the need for future dialysis, was reassured that there is 
no need for dialysis at this time, and that she should continue 
to focus on good blood pressure and blood glucose control to 
help preserve her renal function.  

Her outpatient providers were updated on her hospital course and 
the above changes to her medication regimen.

=================
CHRONIC CARE
=================
# history of heart failure with preserved EF: most recent TTE 
with EF 55% (___). Patient appeared euvolemic, and her 
torsemide, irbesartan were held. carvedilol was continued, and 
amlodipine added for BP control as noted above

# CAD: s/p BMS, ___, recently started on IMDUR on prior 
admission and carvedilol for possible demand ischemia last 
hosptialization (negative nuclear stress). Imdur was 
discontinued. She was started on amlodipine and continued on 
carvedilol, aspirin, and simvastatin.   
 
# HTN: Imdur was stopped (not a good BP med) and switched to 
amlodipine.  ___ not started due to hyperkalemia, and 
thiazide diuretic not started due to propensity to develop 
hyponatremia
  
# T2DM: Blood sugar well-controlled in house, continued Lantus

# Crohn's disease: quiescent, continued sulfasalazine, cipro

====================

nephrologist
- MEDICATION CHANGES: Torsemide 5 mg every other day, 
discontinue irbesartan, Imdur, and sodium bicarb. Start 
amlodipine 5 mg QD

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___, 

It was pleasure taking care of you during your hospitalization 
at ___. You were admitted 
because your sodium level was found to be low and your potassium 
level was high. You had been admitted for similar problems 
during prior hospitalizations. The reason for your low sodium 
and high potassium was likely multifactorial of using torsemide, 
sodium bicarbonate, and irbesartan, all of which were held 
during your hospitalization. We also gave you some normal saline 
IV fluids. The next day, your sodium level returned to ___ 
potassium decreased to 4.8, which is around your baseline 
levels. 

We recommend that you take your torsemide every other day, stop 
taking sodium bicarbonate, and stop taking irbesartan, stop 
taking imdur and that you follow up with your primary care 
doctor. Yoi will start a new blood pressure medication called 
amlodipine. Please also monitor your weights every morning and 
call your doctor if your weight goes up by more than 3 lbs.
